result.title: Look Closer, Look Back, or Wait for Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
result.summary: Streaming video models must answer questions about a live video under strict memory and latency limits. Feeding only the latest few frames keeps present perception sharp, whereas adding past frames dilutes attention on the current scene and triggers hallucinations. Recent cascade methods retrieve past frames when uncertain, but they still fail when current frames are blurry or when decisive future clues have not appeared yet. We introduce ActiveForager, a streaming video agent that maintains a clean short working window and gathers extra evidence only on demand. For each query, the agent either answers directly, zooms into high-resolution recent frames, recalls past events from memory, or waits for upcoming frames. When recalling history, a shared-weight sub-agent verifies candidate clips in isolation and returns a compact evidence summary. A stream-decoupled attention mask then keeps historical evidence from interfering with present visual tokens. We train this policy using counterfactual information gain, which rewards a tool call only when the gathered evidence makes the true answer more likely and prevents tool collapse across all actions. Across Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B on OVO-Bench, ActiveForager improves real-time perception, historical recall, and proactive response at once, lifting overall accuracy on Qwen3-VL-8B from 47.6% to 65.9%. It also doubles zero-shot accuracy on the multi-hop Video-Holmes benchmark while adding minimal visual tokens per query.

AI.brief_summary: 研究流式视频问答中「看清当前、回看历史还是等待未来帧」的证据获取策略，提出 ActiveForager：维持干净短工作窗，按查询按需放大近期帧、回忆过去或等待后续帧，并用反事实信息增益训练该选择策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 式的证据获取与停止决策直接相关；其反事实信息增益对工具调用的监督、以及 stream-decoupled attention mask 抑制历史证据干扰，可供核查是否能迁移到 latent 推理状态。
